title_en: Regulations on the Administration of Kindergartens

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of strengthening the administration of kindergartens and promoting the development of preschool education.
Article 2 These Regulations shall apply to kindergartens that enroll preschool children aged three years or older and provide them with nursing care and education.
Article 3 The nursing care and education work of a kindergarten shall promote the harmonious development of children in the aspects of physique, intelligence, morality, and aesthetics.

Article 4 Local people's governments at all levels shall, in light of the socio-economic development conditions of their respective regions, formulate development plans for kindergartens.
The establishment of kindergartens shall be commensurate with the local resident population.
The development plans for kindergartens in townships, towns, districts under the jurisdiction of cities, and cities without districts shall include a layout scheme for the establishment of kindergartens.

Article 5 Local people's governments at all levels may establish kindergartens pursuant to these Regulations, and shall encourage and support enterprises, institutions, social organizations, residents' committees, villagers' committees, and citizens to establish kindergartens or donate funds for the establishment of kindergartens.

Article 6 The administration of kindergartens shall follow the principles of local responsibility, graded management, and division of responsibilities among relevant departments.
The State Education Commission shall be in charge of the kindergarten administration work nationwide; the education administrative departments of local people's governments at all levels shall be in charge of the kindergarten administration work within their respective administrative regions.

Article 7 A person establishing a kindergarten must locate the kindergarten in a safe area.
It is strictly forbidden to establish a kindergarten in a polluted area or a dangerous area.

Article 8 A person establishing a kindergarten must have premises and facilities that meet the requirements for nursing care and education.
The premises and facilities of a kindergarten must comply with the national hygiene standards and safety standards.

Article 9 A person establishing a kindergarten shall have nursing care, preschool education, medical, and other staff who meet the following conditions:
(1) The kindergarten principal and teachers shall have graduated from a preschool teachers' school (including the preschool education major of vocational schools) or have passed the assessment of the education administrative department.
(2) Doctors shall have graduated from a medical college, and medical assistants and nurses shall have graduated from a secondary health school or have obtained qualification recognition from the health administrative department.
(3) Health workers shall have graduated from senior high school and have received training in child health care.
(4) Nursing staff shall have graduated from junior high school and have received vocational training in child care.
Persons with chronic infectious diseases or mental diseases shall not work in kindergartens.

Article 10 The unit or individual establishing a kindergarten must have a source of funds for carrying out nursing care and education, as well as for maintaining, expanding, or rebuilding the premises and facilities of the kindergarten.
Article 11 The State shall implement a registration system for kindergartens. Without registration, no unit or individual may establish a kindergarten.

Article 12 The establishment and closure of kindergartens in cities shall be registered with the education administrative department of the district people's government or the people's government of a city without districts.
The establishment and closure of kindergartens in rural areas shall be registered with the township or town people's government where they are located, and shall be reported to the education administrative department of the county people's government for the record.

Article 13 A kindergarten shall implement the principle of combining nursing care with education, create a harmonious environment suitable for the education and development of children, and guide the healthy development of children's personalities.
A kindergarten shall safeguard children's physical health, cultivate their good living and hygiene habits, promote their intellectual development, and foster their love for the motherland as well as good moral character and conduct.
Article 14 The enrollment and class grouping of a kindergarten shall comply with the provisions of the education administrative department.

Article 15 A kindergarten shall use putonghua (common speech) which is generally used nationwide. A kindergarten that mainly enrolls children of ethnic minorities may use the language commonly used by that ethnic group.

Article 16 A kindergarten shall take games as the basic form of activity.
A kindergarten may arrange and select educational contents and methods according to its actual conditions, but shall not carry out activities that violate the laws of preschool education or harm children's physical and mental health.
Article 17 It is strictly forbidden to subject children to corporal punishment or disguised corporal punishment.
Article 18 A kindergarten shall establish a health care system to prevent the occurrence of food poisoning and the spread of infectious diseases.

Article 19 A kindergarten shall establish a safety protection system. It is strictly forbidden to set up dangerous buildings and facilities that threaten children's safety within the kindergarten, and it is strictly forbidden to use toxic or harmful substances to make teaching aids and toys.

Article 20 When food poisoning or an epidemic of infectious disease occurs in a kindergarten, the unit or individual establishing the kindergarten shall immediately take emergency rescue measures and promptly report to the local education administrative department or health administrative department.

Article 21 When the premises and facilities of a kindergarten are likely to become dangerous, the unit or individual establishing the kindergarten shall take measures to eliminate the danger and prevent the occurrence of accidents.

Article 22 Education administrative departments at all levels shall be responsible for supervising, evaluating, and guiding the nursing care and education work of kindergartens, organizing the training of kindergarten teachers, examining and verifying the qualifications of kindergarten teachers, and assisting health administrative departments in inspecting and guiding the health care work of kindergartens, and shall, jointly with construction administrative departments, formulate standards for kindergarten premises and facilities.

Article 23 The principal of a kindergarten shall be responsible for the work of the kindergarten.
The principal of a kindergarten shall be appointed by the unit or individual establishing the kindergarten, and shall be reported to the registration authority of the kindergarten for the record.
Teachers, doctors, health workers, nursing staff, and other staff of a kindergarten shall be appointed by the principal of the kindergarten, or may be appointed by the unit or individual establishing the kindergarten.

Article 24 A kindergarten may, in accordance with the fee collection standards formulated by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, collect nursing care fees and education fees from children's parents.
A kindergarten shall strengthen financial management and use all funds rationally. No unit or individual may deduct or misappropriate the funds of a kindergarten.

Article 25 No unit or individual may encroach upon or damage the premises and facilities of a kindergarten, set up buildings or facilities that are dangerous, polluting, or that affect the lighting of a kindergarten around it, or disrupt the normal work order of a kindergarten.

Article 29 A party that refuses to accept an administrative penalty may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice of penalty, apply for a review to the authority at the next higher level of the authority that made the penalty decision; if the party refuses to accept the review decision, it may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the review decision, initiate a lawsuit in the People's Court. If a party neither applies for review nor initiates a lawsuit in the People's Court within the time limit nor complies with the penalty decision, the authority that made the penalty decision shall apply to the People's Court for compulsory enforcement.

Article 30 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate implementing measures in accordance with these Regulations.
Article 31 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the State Education Commission.
Article 32 These Regulations shall come into force as of February 1, 1990.
